subject: social-sciences-sp
description: Social Sciences Senior Phase (Grades 7–9). CAPS-aligned. One subject, two disciplines (History + Geography), each taught every term. All skills open once the grade is selected (gate NONE).

levels.title: Grade 7 — Social Sciences
levels.description: Grade 7 History and Geography (CAPS Senior Phase). Four History topics and four Geography topics, one per term.

tiers.title: History · Term 1: The kingdom of Mali & Timbuktu
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T1 — History. The kingdom of Mali & Timbuktu.

atomic_skills.title: Trade across the Sahara
atomic_skills.description: Camel caravans, the goods traded (gold, salt, ivory, enslaved people) and the spread of Islam into West Africa.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Trade across the Sahara".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Picture the caravan route: salt comes south, gold goes north.

atomic_skills.title: The kingdom of Mali
atomic_skills.description: Mali at its height under Mansa Musa, his pilgrimage to Mecca and the building of the Great Mosque.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The kingdom of Mali".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mansa Musa = Mali's richest king, famous for his hajj to Mecca.

atomic_skills.title: The city of Timbuktu
atomic_skills.description: Timbuktu as a trade centre and a centre of learning, the manuscripts, and why it is a World Heritage Site.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The city of Timbuktu".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Timbuktu was famous for two things: trade AND books/learning.

tiers.title: History · Term 2: The Transatlantic slave trade
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T2 — History. The Transatlantic slave trade.

atomic_skills.title: West Africa & slavery before Europeans
atomic_skills.description: What West African societies were like, and the nature of slavery there before the European trade.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "West Africa & slavery before Europeans".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Slavery existed before Europeans, but the Atlantic trade was far larger and harsher.

atomic_skills.title: Slavery in the American South
atomic_skills.description: Plantations (cotton, sugar, tobacco, rice), why enslaved labour was used, capture, sale and the Middle Passage.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Slavery in the American South".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Follow the chain: captured in West Africa → Middle Passage → sold → plantation.

atomic_skills.title: Impact on enslaved people
atomic_skills.description: Plantation life, slave culture, resistance and rebellion — Nat Turner, the Amistad, the Underground Railroad, Harriet Tubman.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Impact on enslaved people".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Resistance ranged from quiet (go-slow) to open revolt and escape.

atomic_skills.title: Impact on economies
atomic_skills.description: Gains for America and Britain versus the lasting damage done to West Africa.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Impact on economies".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: One side grew rich; the other lost people and wealth.

tiers.title: History · Term 3: Colonisation of the Cape (17th–18th C)
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T3 — History. Colonisation of the Cape (17th–18th C).

atomic_skills.title: Indigenous peoples of the Cape
atomic_skills.description: The Khoikhoi, San and African farmers living at and beyond the Cape before Dutch settlement.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Indigenous peoples of the Cape".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Khoikhoi = herders, San = hunter-gatherers, African farmers = further east.

atomic_skills.title: Dutch settlement and the VOC
atomic_skills.description: Why the VOC set up a refreshment station in 1652, free burghers and French Huguenot immigration.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Dutch settlement and the VOC".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The VOC came for a supply stop on the way to the East, not to farm.

atomic_skills.title: Slavery at the Cape
atomic_skills.description: Where the enslaved came from, conditions, resistance and the legacy (Islam, the Afrikaans language).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Slavery at the Cape".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Cape slaves came mostly from the East and Africa — not the Atlantic trade.

atomic_skills.title: Expanding frontiers and dispossession
atomic_skills.description: Trekboers moving inland, land dispossession, and the Genadendal mission station.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Expanding frontiers and dispossession".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: As settlers moved inland, indigenous people lost land and independence.

tiers.title: History · Term 4: Conflict on the Cape frontiers (early 19th C)
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T4 — History. Conflict on the Cape frontiers (early 19th C).

atomic_skills.title: British arrival and expanding settlement
atomic_skills.description: The British takeover of the Cape and the growth of European settlement in the early 1800s.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Conflict on the Cape frontiers (early 19th C)

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "British arrival and expanding settlement".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Power shifted from the Dutch VOC to Britain.

atomic_skills.title: The eastern frontier
atomic_skills.description: Frontier wars and Xhosa resistance — Chief Maqoma, Andries Stockenström, 1820 settlers and the Great Trek.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Conflict on the Cape frontiers (early 19th C)

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The eastern frontier".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The eastern frontier = repeated wars between settlers and the Xhosa.

atomic_skills.title: The northern frontier
atomic_skills.description: Trade on the northern frontier — the Kora and Griqua, the Tswana towns, and missionaries like Robert Moffat.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Conflict on the Cape frontiers (early 19th C)

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The northern frontier".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Northern frontier = trade and mission contact, not just war.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 1: Map skills (local maps)
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T1 — Geography. Map skills (local maps).

atomic_skills.title: Local and street maps
atomic_skills.description: Finding places on a local map, and using an index and grid to locate places in a street guide.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Local and street maps".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Grid reference: read along the bottom first, then up the side.

atomic_skills.title: Sketch maps and routes
atomic_skills.description: Drawing a simple sketch map, showing compass directions and describing a route.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Sketch maps and routes".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A good sketch map needs a key, a scale and a north arrow.

atomic_skills.title: Distance and scale
atomic_skills.description: Line and word scales, and measuring straight and winding distances on a map.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Distance and scale".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use string for a winding road, a ruler for a straight line, then read the scale.

atomic_skills.title: Places in the news
atomic_skills.description: Locating places in the news on a world map using latitude and longitude.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Places in the news".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Latitude = how far north/south; longitude = how far east/west.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 2: Volcanoes, earthquakes & floods
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T2 — Geography. Volcanoes, earthquakes & floods.

atomic_skills.title: Structure of the earth
atomic_skills.description: The core, mantle and crust, and how the crust moves on tectonic plates.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Structure of the earth".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Three layers: crust (thin skin), mantle (thick middle), core (hot centre).

atomic_skills.title: Volcanoes
atomic_skills.description: Where volcanoes occur in the world and why they form along plate boundaries.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Volcanoes".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Volcanoes line up along the edges of tectonic plates.

atomic_skills.title: Earthquakes
atomic_skills.description: Causes and effects of earthquakes, why some communities are at higher risk, and how to reduce the impact.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Earthquakes".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Earthquakes happen where plates grind past each other.

atomic_skills.title: Floods
atomic_skills.description: Causes of floods (heavy rain, land use), their effects, and how communities prepare and respond.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Floods".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Floods worsen when land can't soak up or carry away the water.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 3: Population growth & change
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T3 — Geography. Population growth & change.

atomic_skills.title: Population concepts
atomic_skills.description: Birth rate, death rate, growth rate, infant mortality and life expectancy.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Population concepts".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Growth rate = births minus deaths (ignoring migration).

atomic_skills.title: Factors affecting birth and death rates
atomic_skills.description: How disease, economic status, beliefs, conflict and government policy change birth and death rates.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Factors affecting birth and death rates".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ask of each factor: does it push births/deaths up or down?

atomic_skills.title: World population growth
atomic_skills.description: Reading the world population graph from 1 AD to today, and what drove the rapid rise.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "World population growth".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Population stayed flat for ages, then shot up with food, medicine and sanitation.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 4: Natural resources & conservation (SA)
tiers.description: CAPS G7 T4 — Geography. Natural resources & conservation (SA).

atomic_skills.title: Natural resources
atomic_skills.description: Earth's natural resources (water, air, soil, forests, animal and marine life) and their use and abuse.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Natural resources".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A natural resource is something useful we take from nature.

atomic_skills.title: Management and conservation
atomic_skills.description: Conservation, conservation areas and marine reserves, community projects and eco-tourism.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Management and conservation".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Conservation = using and protecting resources so they last.

atomic_skills.title: Water in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Who uses South Africa's water, its availability, catchment care and wetlands.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Water in South Africa".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: South Africa is a dry country — water is a scarce, shared resource.

levels.title: Grade 8 — Social Sciences
levels.description: Grade 8 History and Geography (CAPS Senior Phase). Four History topics and four Geography topics, one per term.

tiers.title: History · Term 1: The Industrial Revolution (Britain & southern Africa)
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T1 — History. The Industrial Revolution (Britain & southern Africa).

atomic_skills.title: Changes during the Industrial Revolution in Britain
atomic_skills.description: From a farming and cottage-industry economy to factories — urbanisation, working-class life, child labour and trade unions.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Changes during the Industrial Revolution in Britain".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Industrial Revolution = work moves from home/farm to factories and cities.

atomic_skills.title: Southern Africa by 1860
atomic_skills.description: Indentured labour brought from India to the sugar plantations of Natal, and why.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Southern Africa by 1860".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Indenture = a fixed-term work contract, not slavery but very harsh.

atomic_skills.title: Diamond mining in Kimberley
atomic_skills.description: The 1867 diamond discovery, the move to deep mining, monopoly and the formation of De Beers.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Diamond mining in Kimberley".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Diamonds pulled Britain deeper into controlling South Africa.

tiers.title: History · Term 2: The Mineral Revolution in South Africa
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T2 — History. The Mineral Revolution in South Africa.

atomic_skills.title: Labour control and land expansion
atomic_skills.description: Closed compounds, migrant labour, and the defeat of African kingdoms (Xhosa, Pedi, Zulu).
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The Mineral Revolution in South Africa

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Labour control and land expansion".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mines needed cheap, controllable labour — so independence was crushed.

atomic_skills.title: Deep-level gold mining on the Witwatersrand
atomic_skills.description: The 1886 gold discovery, mining conditions, the Randlords, migrant labour and the rise of Johannesburg.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The Mineral Revolution in South Africa

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Deep-level gold mining on the Witwatersrand".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Gold was deep and expensive — it needed big companies and many workers.

atomic_skills.title: The Mineral Revolution as a turning point
atomic_skills.description: How mining shifted power: Union 1910, the SANNC (later the ANC) 1912 and the 1913 Land Act.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The Mineral Revolution in South Africa

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The Mineral Revolution as a turning point".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Minerals reshaped power, land and labour for the whole 20th century.

tiers.title: History · Term 3: The Scramble for Africa
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T3 — History. The Scramble for Africa.

atomic_skills.title: European colonisation of Africa
atomic_skills.description: The Berlin Conference 1884, the causes of colonisation, and why Europe could colonise Africa so fast.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "European colonisation of Africa".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Europe carved up Africa on a map — Africans were not consulted.

atomic_skills.title: Case study: the Ashanti kingdom
atomic_skills.description: The Ashanti, their contact with Europeans, and the British colonisation of the Gold Coast (Ghana).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Case study: the Ashanti kingdom".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use the Ashanti as one detailed example of the wider Scramble.

tiers.title: History · Term 4: World War I (1914–1918)
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T4 — History. World War I (1914–1918).

atomic_skills.title: Why World War I broke out
atomic_skills.description: Long-term causes (nationalism, empires, alliances, arms) and the spark at Sarajevo; Allies vs Central Powers.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Why World War I broke out".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Long-term tension + one assassination = war.

atomic_skills.title: Experiences of World War I
atomic_skills.description: Trench warfare, conscription and propaganda, and South Africa's part — Delville Wood and the sinking of the Mendi.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Experiences of World War I".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The war was fought in trenches and felt at home through conscription.

atomic_skills.title: Women in Britain during World War I
atomic_skills.description: Changing roles of women in the workplace and the campaign for the vote.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Women in Britain during World War I".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: With men at the front, women filled the factories — and demanded the vote.

atomic_skills.title: The defeat of Germany and the Treaty of Versailles
atomic_skills.description: Germany's defeat and the punishing terms of the 1919 treaty (picked up again in Grade 9).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The defeat of Germany and the Treaty of Versailles".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Versailles punished Germany harshly — which mattered later.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 1: Maps & globes
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T1 — Geography. Maps & globes.

atomic_skills.title: Maps and atlases
atomic_skills.description: Latitude and longitude in degrees and minutes, the atlas index, and line, word and ratio scales.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Maps and atlases".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ratio scale 1:50 000 means 1 cm on the map = 50 000 cm on the ground.

atomic_skills.title: The globe
atomic_skills.description: Time zones and the date line, the earth's tilt, and how the earth's revolution makes the seasons.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The globe".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Day/night = spin; seasons = tilt + orbit around the sun.

atomic_skills.title: Satellite images
atomic_skills.description: What satellite images show — water, vegetation, land use and cloud — and how they are used.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Satellite images".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Satellite images are photos from space, read by colour and pattern.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 2: Climate regions
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T2 — Geography. Climate regions.

atomic_skills.title: Factors influencing temperature and rainfall
atomic_skills.description: Latitude, distance from the sea, altitude, ocean currents and mountains.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Factors influencing temperature and rainfall".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Five controls: latitude, sea, height, currents, mountains.

atomic_skills.title: South Africa's climate
atomic_skills.description: How those factors shape temperature and rainfall across South African centres.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "South Africa's climate".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Compare coastal vs inland, high vs low, east vs west.

atomic_skills.title: Climate around the world
atomic_skills.description: Weather vs climate, the elements of weather, the main climate types and a world climate map.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Climate around the world".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Weather = today; climate = the long-run average.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 3: Settlement & urbanisation
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T3 — Geography. Settlement & urbanisation.

atomic_skills.title: Settlement and land use
atomic_skills.description: Urban land-use zones (CBD, industry, residential) and types of rural settlement.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Settlement and land use".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A city has zones: business centre, industry, and where people live.

atomic_skills.title: Land use on aerial photographs
atomic_skills.description: Reading oblique and vertical aerial photos to identify natural and built features and land use.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Land use on aerial photographs".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Vertical photo = straight down (like a map); oblique = at an angle.

atomic_skills.title: Urbanisation
atomic_skills.description: Why cities grow — push and pull migration — and the social issues of rapid growth in South Africa.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Urbanisation".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Push = reasons to leave the country; pull = reasons cities attract people.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 4: Transport & trade
tiers.description: CAPS G8 T4 — Geography. Transport & trade.

atomic_skills.title: Trade and transport around the world
atomic_skills.description: Why people trade, the link between trade and transport, and the modes (sea, air, road, rail, pipeline).

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Trade and transport around the world".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Trade needs transport — match the goods to the best mode.

atomic_skills.title: Trade and transport in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: South Africa's roads, railways, airports and harbours, with a harbour case study.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Trade and transport in South Africa".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Harbours connect South African exports to the world.

atomic_skills.title: People and transport in urban areas
atomic_skills.description: Public and private commuter transport, transport problems and public-transit solutions.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "People and transport in urban areas".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Think of the daily commute: cost, congestion and pollution.

levels.title: Grade 9 — Social Sciences
levels.description: Grade 9 History and Geography (CAPS Senior Phase). Four History topics and four Geography topics, one per term.

tiers.title: History · Term 1: World War II (1919–1945)
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T1 — History. World War II (1919–1945).

atomic_skills.title: The rise of Nazi Germany
atomic_skills.description: The Weimar Republic's failure, Hitler and the Nazis, the Depression, the Nuremberg Laws and the fascist state.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The rise of Nazi Germany".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Weak democracy + economic crisis = the opening Hitler used.

atomic_skills.title: World War II in Europe
atomic_skills.description: The outbreak of war, the Holocaust and the 'Final Solution', resistance, and the war's end in Europe.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "World War II in Europe".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Two threads: the fighting, and the genocide of the Holocaust.

atomic_skills.title: World War II in the Pacific
atomic_skills.description: Pearl Harbour and America's entry, Japanese expansion, and the internment of Japanese Americans.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "World War II in the Pacific".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Pearl Harbour (1941) pulled the USA into the war against Japan.

tiers.title: History · Term 2: The Nuclear Age & the Cold War
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T2 — History. The Nuclear Age & the Cold War.

atomic_skills.title: Tension after World War II
atomic_skills.description: Growing distrust between the USSR (communism) and the USA and the West (capitalism).
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The Nuclear Age & the Cold War

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Tension after World War II".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Allies in war became rivals in peace: communism vs capitalism.

atomic_skills.title: Atomic bombs and the Nuclear Age
atomic_skills.description: How the war ended in the Pacific, why the USA dropped the bombs, and whether it was justified.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The Nuclear Age & the Cold War

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Atomic bombs and the Nuclear Age".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Hiroshima and Nagasaki ended the war and opened the nuclear age.

atomic_skills.title: The Cold War: areas of conflict
atomic_skills.description: The arms race, the space race, and the division of Germany and the Berlin Wall.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The Nuclear Age & the Cold War

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The Cold War: areas of conflict".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 'Cold' War = rivalry and proxy contests, not direct superpower fighting.

atomic_skills.title: The end of the Cold War
atomic_skills.description: The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 and the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The Nuclear Age & the Cold War

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "The end of the Cold War".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 1989 the Wall falls; 1991 the USSR breaks up.

tiers.title: History · Term 3: Turning points: 1948 & the 1950s
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T3 — History. Turning points: 1948 & the 1950s.

atomic_skills.title: Human rights and the myth of race
atomic_skills.description: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, human evolution and common ancestry, and why 'race' is not biological.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Human rights and the myth of race".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 1948 didn't invent segregation — it made it total law.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 1: Map skills (topographic & orthophoto)
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T1 — Geography. Map skills (topographic & orthophoto).

atomic_skills.title: Contour lines
atomic_skills.description: What contour lines show, reading steep and gentle slopes, and spotting river valleys and spurs.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Contour lines".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Contours close together = steep; far apart = gentle.

atomic_skills.title: Orthophoto maps
atomic_skills.description: Vertical aerial photos turned into orthophoto maps and how height is shown on them.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Orthophoto maps".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An orthophoto is a photo corrected to map scale, with contours added.

atomic_skills.title: Topographic maps
atomic_skills.description: Reading 1:50 000 map symbols, height clues, contour patterns, scale, distance and coordinates.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Topographic maps".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Learn the symbol key first — then everything else reads off it.

atomic_skills.title: Interpreting maps and photographs
atomic_skills.description: Cross-referencing maps and photos to describe landscape, land use and settlement patterns.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Interpreting maps and photographs".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Combine sources: the map gives height, the photo gives detail.

tiers.title: Geography · Term 2: Development issues
tiers.description: CAPS G9 T2 — Geography. Development issues.

atomic_skills.title: Meaning and measuring development
atomic_skills.description: Economic, social and environmental development, and measuring it with the Human Development Index.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Meaning and measuring development".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: HDI blends income, education and life expectancy into one score.

atomic_skills.description: Why countries differ — history (colonialism), trade, technology, health, education and stability.

error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: No single cause — development comes from many factors together.

atomic_skills.title: Opportunities for development
atomic_skills.description: Fairer trade, alternatives to industrialisation and sustainable development.

error_signatures.description: A common misunderstanding when learning "Opportunities for development".
error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Development should also be fair and sustainable, not just bigger.

error_signatures.example: Authoring note: replace with the specific misconception once items are written.

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Bare, overworked soil washes or blows away fastest.
